story: A selected workspace visit loads code and a fresh live-authorized GET together; an Auth epoch already superseded before the effect commits must send no obsolete read, and a later real change must still refresh.

reactReview.stableCallback: useCallback has no dependencies and reads the provider-owned current epoch ref.
reactReview.refWrites: Only the existing SDK notification invalidation branch synchronously publishes a new opaque object; not during render.
reactReview.effectOwnership: Effect retains mounted cleanup and complete memoized owner; epoch and stable comparator are dependencies. Current-scope code and GET retain Promise.all.
reactReview.resultSettlement: Both fulfillment and rejection check current mount and epoch. Existing owner equality controls rendering across user, support, club, privacy, mode, retry and Demo changes.
reactReview.eventRule: Existing token-change/INITIAL_SESSION predicate and subscription cleanup unchanged.
reactReview.unchangedUI: No new controls, icons, loading delays, layout, focus behavior, draft ownership or new dependency.

fullStoryEvidence.evidence: tests/live.log: real selected screens, mobile/pointer navigation, rapid switching and native GET overlap pass; final new browser regression passes three constrained entries in tests/live-followup.log.
lib/workspace-read.ts and app/api/workspace/route.ts unchanged in 913-file manifests. Existing unit/live strict kind/argument allowlists, no-store and same-origin handling pass.

fullStoryEvidence.boundary: GET to live authority and database
fullStoryEvidence.evidence: tests/live.log retains membership/capability/suspension/account/session/recovery/revocation and metadata parity coverage; tests/security.log has three native concurrency passes.

tests/unit-focused-fixed.log covers current mount, pre-commit success/error fence, Demo and support/privacy ownership. tests/live-followup.log confirms fresh revisit and no old content on captured revoked cookies.

limitations: The initial live suite has66 passes and one test-selector failure, resolved by a targeted followup on the same frozen build; no full-suite clean67 claim.
Existing tests and loopback fixtures establish covered behavior, not exhaustive formal security proof or production latency.
No additional builds or tests were launched by this experiment during collection; external development overlap was discovered during cleanup and recorded as a latency confound.
